locator: Alex O'Connor, "Frank Turek thinks that Evil proves God's existence" (Alex O'Connor, 2016-08-23), 01:56–02:06: the evil that people refer to when they try to criticize the idea of an omni benevolent God
interpretation: Bridge reading of the same span: in answering a moral argument, O'Connor places the evil the critic invokes among the matters of morality whose objectivity he denies, so the evil premise counts as a moral statement and not as a report of non-evaluative fact (such as that there is pain). A critic who restates the premise in non-evaluative terms would need a further moral premise to reach the conclusion, which would then be the moral statement in question; that variant is not this claim.
